Both references agree. Now let's test larger FIBs (e.g., 5000, 20000, 200000) against the fast reference, and large traces (1M).

Let me create a bigger stress driver for large cases.

arguments.command:
cat > /work/tmp/big.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
set -u
BIN=/work/submit/planb64
T=/work/tmp
seed=$1; nfib=$2; ntr=$3
python3 $T/gen.py $seed $nfib $ntr $T/bfib.txt $T/btrace.txt
/usr/bin/time -f "build cpp %e s %M KB" $BIN build $T/bfib.txt $T/bgot.idx
/usr/bin/time -f "build ref %e s %M KB" python3 $T/ref.py build $T/bfib.txt > $T/bref.idx
cmp $T/bgot.idx $T/bref.idx && echo "BIG IDX OK ($nfib)"
for m in scalar "batch 256" "batch 007"; do
  /usr/bin/time -f "lookup cpp $m %e s %M KB" $BIN lookup $T/bgot.idx $T/btrace.txt $m > $T/bgot.out
done
python3 $T/ref.py lookup $T/bref.idx $T/btrace.txt > $T/bref.out
$BIN lookup $T/bgot.idx $T/btrace.txt batch 256 > $T/bgot2.out
$BIN lookup $T/bgot.idx $T/btrace.txt batch 007 > $T/bgot3.out
cmp $T/bgot.out $T/bref.out && cmp $T/bgot2.out $T/bref.out && cmp $T/bgot3.out $T/bref.out && echo "BIG OUT OK ($ntr)"
EOF
chmod +x /work/tmp/big.sh
cd /work/tmp && ./big.sh 777 5000 20000
